reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `slug-validation` (`e8612a7`) against `main` (`9ba0eca`). Two findings:

1. *High — validation accepts invalid characters anywhere around a valid substring.*  
   `src/validate.js:1–4`: `/[a-z0-9-]+/` checks for a match, not that the whole string conforms. Confirmed `UPPERabc`, `hello world`, `a/b`, `../admin`, and `"hello\n"` all pass validation and `pagePath`. URL encoding doesn’t enforce the slug policy—it just encodes the invalid input. Require a full-string match, including rejection of trailing line terminators.

2. *Medium — reserved slugs aren’t enforced on the page path.*  
   `src/route.js:4–5`: `pagePath` only calls `isValidSlug`; neither function checks `isReserved`. All four reserved names (`new`, `edit`, `admin`, `api`) are accepted—for example, `pagePath('admin')` returns `/p/admin`, contrary to the documented restriction. Enforce the reserved-name check before returning a page URL.

*Tests:* All 4 existing tests pass, but none exercise invalid-character rejection or `pagePath`. Add regression tests for the bypasses above and rejection of all four reserved names through `pagePath`.

No code changed; working tree is clean.
